meta.title: Ondra Theater
meta.description: Multi-character theater for Ondra (L9 extension pool): it answers exactly one question — when several characters share a scene, who speaks next? What it hands out is stage direction, not lines: who is on stage, whose turn it is, what intent this turn carries (open, respond, bridge, close), the sentence cap, and what must not be done. Four rulings are written into types and constants. No character may speak twice in a row (otherwise the theater silently degrades into a monologue, so fewer than two characters is refused outright). The cast is hard-capped at four (anything larger is refused on the spot rather than queued, because a queue lets the extra character suddenly speak several rounds later). Every scene must carry a closing condition (a round cap plus a silence criterion; either one ends the scene, so nothing can run forever). And leaving the stage requires closing it first — there is no leave method at all, so removing a character means closing and reopening, which makes a mid-scene disappearance impossible at the interface level. Rotation is deterministic: seat order is speaking order, and the previous speaker is always skipped, so there is no randomness and no loudest-voice-wins. Reading never advances; only the side that actually spoke records the turn, so a shell may poll freely without pushing the same character up twice. No persona assembly (that belongs to the persona core), no line generation (that belongs to the expression chain), no dialogue driving (that belongs to the dialogue service), no UI, no timers, and no persistence — a scene is disposable, and a restart ends it, because by the time it resumes the audience has changed.
